chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

There is no omission (sahw) upon the Imam (prayer leader), nor is there an omission upon the one who prays behind the Imam, nor is there an omission upon the omission, nor a repetition upon the repetition.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on forgetfulness (sahw) for the Imam and follower in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the principle of 'sahw al-sahw' (forgetfulness of forgetfulness), establishing that the Imam and followers are exempt from the penalty of repeating acts for minor omissions or doubts in prayer. It reflects the Shia juristic view that the chain of obligation is not broken by successive layers of forgetfulness, ensuring the validity of the prayer without excessive rigor. This ruling underscores the divine ease in worship, contrasting with stricter interpretations that might require multiple repetitions for cumulative errors.
